title: Stalks of finite type module sheaves are finite modules
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F an O_X-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and x a point of X. Then the actual stalk F_x [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] is a finitely generated module over the structure-ring stalk O_{X,x}.

source.place: Stacks Project Tag 01B4, Definition 01B5: finite local generators; restriction-stalk transport

proof.text: Choose a finite local generating family near x. Transport its generating epimorphism through overEquiv to the open subscheme and through overFunctorEquiv to the restricted F. The covering condition gives an open U containing x.
Apply generating_sections_iff_stalk_span to the finite family on U at the lift y of x. Its finite range spans the whole stalk, so Submodule.fg_span proves this stalk is finite.

The additive restriction-stalk comparison is semilinear over the structure-ring comparison U.stalkIso y. To prove this, represent a scalar and a vector by germs on a common intersection. The germ comparison formulas and smul_restrictAppIso_hom identify the two actions. For the open inclusion its appIso is the identity. The comparison is surjective, so Module.Finite.of_surjective transports finite generation back to F_x. Empty generator sets give the zero module; an empty scheme has no point x.

theorem finite_moduleStalk_of_isFiniteType (X : Scheme.{u}) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteType] (x : X) :

      ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj F)
